title: Original Texas-Style Chili (Bowl of Red)

source.text: Frank X. Tolbert, A Bowl of Red

steps.action: Boil 5 min; cool, stem, seed, and chop. Reserve the cooking water:
items: 3 to 6 ancho chiles (or 3 to 6 Tbsp chili powder or ground chile)

steps.action: Render over medium until the fat runs; discard the solids:
items: 2 oz beef suet (or vegetable oil, for less grease)

steps.action: Sear in the fat, in 2 or 3 batches:
items: 3 lb lean beef, preferably stewing meat

steps.action: Combine in a large pot, with chile water to about 2 in above the meat; boil, then simmer 30 min:
items: Reserved chile water, topped up with water as needed

steps.action: Add, cover, and simmer 45 min, stirring only occasionally:
Skim the grease; taste and adjust seasoning. If not hot enough, add:
items: 2 to 4 ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded, left whole

steps.action: Stir in to thicken; simmer 30 min more, until the meat is tender:

items: Skip the suet; sear in oil
Refrigerate overnight; skim the fat the next day
Add the masa on reheating, only if too thin

edits: Servings not in source; estimated from 3 lb beef
Source does not say how to cut the beef; 1 in cubes or coarse chili grind are typical for this style
Source does not say when to add chili powder if used instead of pods; adding it with the other seasonings is the usual approach
Masa harina can lump if added dry; whisking it with a little of the hot liquid first avoids that (not in source)
Source does not say when Fowler added the tomato sauce
